transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... well, I just can't stop feeling like I'm a danger to people, and a huge disappointment. I'm a registered nurse, and I had a near-miss recently. Ever since then, I just feel like it proves I'm not meant to do this. I honestly feel like everyone would be better off without me around.
Before this near-miss incident at work, how would you say your mood and general outlook on life had been over the past few months or longer?

Well, even before the incident, things really weren't great. Most days I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I go into the clinic and I try to act normal... I'm smiling at my patients in Spanish and doing my job, but honestly, I feel like I'm just barely holding myself together.

When you say things haven't been great for months or longer, have you been feeling this heavy, empty way pretty much every day during that entire time, or have there been periods of weeks or months where your mood was actually better before it got bad again?

Pretty much every day, yeah. I haven't really had any periods of time where things got better. Um... this has actually been going on for about a year and two months now. It all started right after I graduated high school and began my college classes, along with working full-time at the clinic. It's just been that same empty feeling the entire time.

Before this year-and-two-month period that started when you began college, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed or had this same kind of heavy, empty feeling for several weeks or longer?

No, not really. Before I started college, I felt pretty normal. I mean, I had bad days like anyone else in high school, but nothing like this. This heavy feeling... it really just started a little over a year ago. I've never felt this way before that.

Have you ever had a period of time, even just a few days or a week, where your mood was unusually high or energetic—where you felt really good, needed less sleep than usual, or felt like you could do anything?

No, I haven't. I've never really had a time where I felt unusually energetic or anything like that. I usually sleep pretty normally, or at least I try to, but I've definitely never felt like I didn't need sleep or that I could just do anything. It's just been the opposite, really.
During this past year-and-two-months when you've been feeling this heavy, empty way, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight?

Yeah, actually. I just... I forget to eat until late in the day. And then when I finally realize it, I usually just force down some crackers or maybe just have some coffee. I haven't been trying to lose weight at all, but my work pants have definitely been getting pretty loose on me lately.
Over this past year-plus, have you noticed that you're moving or speaking more slowly than you used to, or have people commented that you seem slowed down?

Yeah, I have. People at the clinic where I work have actually asked if I'm tired a lot lately. I guess I'm moving a lot slower when I'm getting supplies and things like that. And... sometimes it just takes me a few seconds to process and answer even really simple questions. So, yeah, people have definitely noticed.

Apart from feeling like a disappointment because of the near-miss at work, do you find yourself feeling guilty or worthless about other things in your life, or do you generally feel like you're not good enough as a person?

Yeah, I mean... it mostly just revolves around that. I just can't stop feeling like I'm a danger and a total disappointment. It's like... that one near-miss just proves that I'm not meant to be a nurse. I just have this constant thought that everyone would be better off without me. So, yeah, I guess it does make me feel like I'm just not good enough as a person overall.
During this year-and-two-months period, have there been any weeks or even just a few days where you felt noticeably better—where that heavy feeling lifted a bit, even if just temporarily?

No, not really. It's just been... a constant thing. I haven't had any days where I woke up and felt like the heavy feeling was gone or even just lighter. It's just been the same every day for the past year or so.
